settlementFee.note: TITLE INSURANCE PREMIUMS in New Mexico are set by the New Mexico Title Insurance Law and promulgated by the OSI, uniform across every title insurer/agent in the state at a given liability amount. This is not a provider-set price and is included here for regulatory context only. NM Form 49 (in OSI's own promulgated-forms packet) states verbatim: 'New Mexico title insurance premium rates are set every other year or approved by the New Mexico Superintendent of Insurance... The Superintendent of Insurance does not regulate other title company charges' -- i.e., OSI itself confirms that settlement/escrow/closing fees are NOT part of the promulgated schedule and are left to the market, which is the segment this survey otherwise focuses on for NM.

settlementFee.cancellationFee: 'Reasonable and appropriate' (not a fixed dollar figure; promulgated table leaves this to case-by-case determination)

bundlingNotes: NM is a promulgated-rate state for title insurance PREMIUMS ONLY: the premium is fixed by the NM Title Insurance Law / OSI at a given liability amount and effective date, cross-verified this session against two independently-sourced provider rate cards (WFG National Title's 2025 card and Centric Title & Escrow's 2022 card) that are numerically IDENTICAL to each other and to the OSI table -- meaning the promulgated rate has not changed between at least 2022 and 2025. A third, older (2012-vintage) Fidelity National Title rate table shows meaningfully HIGHER premiums at every liability tier (e.g., $100,000 -> $831 owner's / $748 90%-loan, vs. $707/$636 in the 2022-2025 tables), which is evidence the promulgated rate was reduced sometime between 2012 and 2022 and then held flat through 2025. Because the premium itself carries no market signal, the settlement/closing/escrow fee entries below (documented separately by provider) are where NM title companies actually compete on price -- OSI's own regulatory text (NM Form 49) explicitly disclaims authority over those charges.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly to Owner's and Loan title insurance premiums statewide, all metros, all provider types (national-brand underwriters and independent agents alike file/use the same promulgated table). Premium depends only on policy liability/face amount, not purchase-vs-refinance transaction type.

itemizedFees.processing: Additional recurring monthly disbursements: $6 each; non-monthly disbursements: $15 each

bundlingNotes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: New Mexico's RLD (Regulation and Licensing Department) licenses 'escrow companies' as a distinct category from title companies, but explicitly EXEMPTS title companies performing real-estate closing/escrow services from that licensing requirement. As a result, the RLD-licensed 'escrow companies' operating in NM (this one and Sunwest Escrow, below) are actually loan-servicing/mortgage-collection businesses that administer ongoing payment streams on seller-financed notes or contracts for deed -- a fundamentally different service and market segment from a real-estate settlement/closing agent's one-time transaction fee. This is analogous in shape to Alaska's AS 21.66.370/460 statutory premium-vs-escrow split (see AK.md) but structurally different: in NM it is a licensing-category carve-out rather than two rate filings for the same type of transaction. This entry is retained in NM.json for completeness and transparency (it is a genuine, dollar-denominated, provider-published fee schedule) but is explicitly EXCLUDED from the real-estate settlement-fee-stack range reported in NM.md.
transactionContext: Ongoing collection-escrow servicing for privately-held notes/contracts for deed, statewide New Mexico. NOT a purchase or refinance real-estate closing transaction.

scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan amount, Bernalillo County (NM's most-populous county per the standard scenario), Property Purchase (with or without financing) transaction type, Residential property type, tool defaults for all other policy questions. No Loan Policy line appeared despite the $400,000 loan amount entered; a $100.00 Title Commitment fee is itemized separately from the premium (this tool's only non-premium settlement-adjacent line item found for NM).
methodology: Driven via plain HTTP POST (Python requests.Session(), not WebFetch -- WebFetch's HTML-to-markdown conversion strips the raw hidden ASP.NET fields needed to replay the postback) against the classic __doPostBack/__VIEWSTATE WebForms flow, replaying the recipe already on file in this project's CALCULATORS.md (FNF family section) and previously used for CT/CO/AR: (1) GET ?ID=FNF&state=NM to capture hidden __VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION fields and the county dropdown; (2) POST the county selection (own __EVENTTARGET); (3) POST the tool's own pre-selected default underwriter plus btnGeneralNext=Next to advance to the Amounts step; (4) POST TranType$ddl=PropertyPurchase (own __EVENTTARGET) to reveal the Purchase Amount field; (5) POST AmountPurchase$txt=500000 and AmountLoan1$txt=400000 together (own __EVENTTARGET on the loan field) to reveal any further conditional questions; (6) auto-answered any newly-revealed required Yes/No radio question with its first listed option, then POST btnFinish=Finish for the final Rate Summary. No personal data fields exist anywhere in this flow (only county/underwriter/transaction-type/dollar-amount fields).
